name: Wastewater treatment; U.S. average treatment; at plant
description:
This process reflects U.S. national average treatment of 1 cubic meter of wastewater. The national average is based on survey reported biological treatment process prevalence and nitrogen and phosphorous effluent quality.

Achieved effluent quality is defined in the technology field. 

Inventory data was generated for a theortical process configuration treating on average 10 million gallons per day of wastewater. Key information is available in process metadata. Full process documentation is available in EPA report number 832-R-21-006A.

System boundaries of the treatment process include energy, chemical, consumable inputs and greenhouse gas emissions for major primary, secondary, tertiary, disinfection and solids treatment processes. Release of treated effluent to surface water and landfill disposal of generated sludge are modeled in separate (linked) processes. Basic infrastructure is also included (excavation, concrete, steel). Operation of the sewage collection system, infrastructure disposal, and electrical and mechanical equipment (e.g. pumps body, control boxes, clarifier scraper arm) are outside of the system boundaries. 

Wastewater treatment processes are available for five levels of treatment performance. Level one is the lowest standard. Level five produces the cleanest effluent.
category: 22: Utilities/2213: Water, Sewage and Other Systems

processDocumentation.timeDescription:
Underlying data is estimated to reflect 2025 technologies. The survey data used to generate the national average treatment process mix reflects 2018. 

Wastewater effluent quality standards will change over time and with geography. Current and future wastewater standards should be reflected in treatment levels establish for the level 1 through level 5 systems. Updating background electricity and input data should maintain process relevance so long as the target treatment system matches the defined system.
processDocumentation.geographyDescription: U.S. Average. Based on 2000 responses from 16,500 surveyed publicly owned wastewater treatment facilities in the U.S.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription:
The national average wastewater treatment technology mix (based on analysis of survey replies) is: Level 1 - 47%, Level 2 - 28%, Level 3 - 25%. 

Level 1: conventional plug flow activated sludge -  Treatment processes include: grit removal, clarifiers, activated sludge biological process, chlorination/dechlorination, gravity thickening, anaerobic digestion and centrifugation.
Level 1 Effluent quality- Suspended solids - 20 mg/L, Biological oxygen demand - 7.7 mg/L, Total nitrogen - 30 mg/L, Total phosphorus - 4.9 mg/L

Level 2-1: anaerobic/anoxic/oxic - Treatment processes include: grit removal, clarifiers, anaerobic/anoxic/oxic biological process, chlorination/dechlorination, gravity thickening, anaerobic digestion and centrifugation.
Level 2 Effluent quality- Suspended solids - 20 mg/L, Biological oxygen demand - 4.7 mg/L, Total nitrogen - 8 mg/L, Total phosphorus - 0.28 mg/L

Level 3-1: 5-stage bardenpho - Treatment processes include: grit removal, clarifiers, fermentation, 5-stage bardenpho biological process, chemical precipitation, sand filtration, chlorination/dechlorination, gravity thickening, anaerobic digestion and centrifugation.
Level 3 Effluent quality- Suspended solids - 8 mg/L, Biological oxygen demand - 2.3 mg/L, Total nitrogen - 6 mg/L, Total phosphorus - 0.2 mg/L"
processDocumentation.modelingConstantsDescription: Facilities reporting 'Activated Sludge Treatment' were classified as level 1. Facilities reporting 'Advanced activated sludge' were classfied as level 2. Facilities reporting other treatment technologies which consisted of options such as 'attached growth', 'natural treatment' and 'oxidation ditch' were classified as level 1. Facilities were also classified as Level 1, 2 or 3 based on reported nutrient effluent quality. Level 2-1 and level 3-1 systems were used to represent level 2 and level 3 treatment, respectively.
processDocumentation.completenessDescription: It was not possible to distinguish Level 4 and Level 5 treatment facilities based on the lowest surveyed effluent categories: <0.3 mg P/L and <5 mg N/L.
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: The national average WWTP process mix is based on a survey conducted by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (U.S. EPA) of 16,500 publicly owned wastewater treatment plants and received >2200 facility responses. All responses to the full survey (approximately 1600) were utilized to estimate the national average technology mix.
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: All facilities in the very small, small, medium and large size classes were categorized as Level 1, 2 or 3 based on treatment technology used, nitrogen effluent quality and phosphorus effluent quality. Not 100% of facilities could be classified based on treatment technology alone.  An average classification was calculated for each size class across these three factors. Across all facility sizes, between 42% and 50% of facilities were classified as level 1, 19%-31% were classified as level 2, and 21%-28% were classified as level 3. Given the consistency across size classes a single average was taken across all size classes and adjusted to equal 100%.
processDocumentation.samplingDescription: Ranges reported in the data treatment field could be used as a source of uncertainty/sensitivity data.
processDocumentation.dataCollectionDescription: Wastewater process data: 2014-2019. Technology prevalence and effluent quality: 2019-2021.
processDocumentation.useAdvice: This is a U.S. average process created based on nutrient effluent quality and treatment technology prevalence and should be used as a source of background wastewater treatment data when more specific understanding of the utilized wastewater treatment technology is unknown. If known within the scope of your assessment, select a representative Level 1 through Level 5 wastewater treatment process based on permit standards for the target wastewater treatment plant and the type of biological process used.
processDocumentation.intendedApplication:
This process is intended to be used as a background process by LCA practitioners, industry and the general public to reflect the impact of wastewater treatment within their product systems. The inventory should be sufficient to model TRACI 2.1 and USETox impact categories.

Situation C2 - Accounting, without system-external interatctions. The intended application is a purely descriptive accounting / documentation of the analysed system excluding existing interactions with other systems in the LCI model.
processDocumentation.projectDescription: Data were prepared by Eastern Research Group (ERG) in their role as curators of the USLCI.
